title: What the ITDR Admin Portal help pages and the SecOps ITDR Config page describe: sign-in and navigation, users and roles, account settings, ITDR Config, tables, queries, Advanced Settings, logs and Investigate

prose.text: The Deception copies of these pages are [[deception.admin-portal]], [[deception.investigate]], [[deception.endpoint-settings]] and [[deception.query-language]]; the ITDR facts are below.

prose.heading: ITDR Config in the SecOps platform

prose.text: {{itdr-config-location}} The overview describes the same configuration differently {{divergence:itdr-config-where-managed}} ([[identity-protection.overview:legacy-redirect]]). {{itdr-config-sections}} {{itdr-config-manage-items}} {{itdr-config-safelists}} ([[identity-protection.safelists]]) {{itdr-config-agent-settings}}
{{advanced-settings-tabs}} {{license-tab-fields}} {{retention-values}} The Evidence file and internal-component sections of the Deception page are not on this page {{gap:advanced-settings-evidence}}.

{{investigate-extended-details-tabs}} Whether the Deception tabs for network and evidence exist in ITDR is not stated {{gap:extended-details-tabs}}. {{investigate-extended-details-elements}} {{investigate-chronology-threatparse}}

checks.do: For the notification categories a user can enable, the ITDR window's License and Security Alerts rather than the Deception categories.
For which containment targets the ITDR Actions menu lists, the five named on the Controlling Threat Events page.
For the tabs on View Extended Details in ITDR, the three the page lists.
For where users are added when Authentication Service is enabled, the ITDR page's Directory > Users path.

user-profile.statement: The ITDR user profile is a name and a time zone, configured when an administrator provisions the account; the name is displayed during specific configurations and used when submitting a ticket to Zscaler Support, and the time zone is used when sending automated email alerts.

quotes: The user profile consists of your name and time zone.
It is configured when an administrator provisions an account for you in the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.
Your name is displayed during specific configurations. It is also used when submitting a ticket to Zscaler Support.
The time zone is used when sending automated email alerts.

change-password.statement: Changing the ITDR password on the Accounts Settings page needs the current password and a confirmed new password; an estimator rates the new password's strength with a color meter (green strong, red weak), and a confirmation email is sent after the change.

quotes: On the Accounts Settings page, under Change Password, enter your Current Password.
Enter your New Password, and then enter it again in the Confirm New Password field.
An estimator is used to determine the password strength.
a green line indicates a strong password and a red line indicates a weak password.
After the password is changed, you will receive a confirmation email.

itdr-config-location.statement: In the Identity Protection documentation, ITDR settings are reached in the SecOps platform at Identities > ITDR Config, but the detailed configuration is managed in the legacy ITDR Admin Portal.

quotes: You can access the ITDR settings for Identity Protection within the Zscaler Security Operations (SecOps) platform (Identities > ITDR Config).
While the ITDR Config page is available on the SecOps platform, the detailed configuration is managed in the legacy Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.

itdr-config-sections.statement: The ITDR Config page has four sections: ITDR Manage, ITDR Settings, Endpoint Settings and Server Agent Settings.

quotes: The ITDR Config page is organized into the following sections:
- ITDR Manage
- ITDR Settings
- Endpoint Settings
- Server Agent Settings

itdr-config-manage-items.statement: ITDR Manage configures identity scans and policies across AD, Entra ID and Okta, and lists AD Posture Scan, AD Privileged Account Tracking, Endpoint Credential Exposure Scan, Entra ID Posture Scan, Threat Detection Policies, Okta, AD Change Detection and Entra Change Detection.

quotes: - ITDR Manage
Configure identity scans and policies for posture, change detection, credential exposure, and identity threats across AD, Entra ID, and Okta.
Active Directory (AD) Posture Scan: You can configure AD posture scans by choosing attributes, selecting domain controllers, defining scan timeouts, and running scans on demand.
Active Directory Privileged Account Tracking: Track high-risk AD accounts by defining which privileged users to monitor for misuse and threats.
Endpoint Credential Exposure Scan: Scan endpoints for exposed credentials and secrets to uncover theft and privilege-escalation risks.
Entra ID Posture Scan: Connect Entra ID tenants, deploy scanners, and run posture checks on identities and configurations.
Threat Detection Policies: Configure and tune threat detection policies to monitor identity attacks, define detection scope, evaluate findings, and protect Active Directory.

Okta: Integrate with Okta to enrich the identity metadata, identify real-time changes to an Okta identity, and perform actions on an Okta identity like activate user, suspend user, clear user sessions, etc.
Active Directory Change Detection: Configure and manage AD change detection policies to monitor critical directory changes and trigger security alerts.
Entra Change Detection: Configure Entra ID change detection policies to track critical directory changes, apply custom rules, and trigger alerts on risky activities.

itdr-config-safelists.statement: ITDR Settings holds eight safelists (AD Issue, AD Object, AD Change Detection Issue, AD Change Detection Object, Entra ID Issue, Entra ID Object, Entra ID Change Detection Issue and Entra ID Change Detection Object) that exclude known, trusted or accepted issues and objects from risk scores and reduce alert noise.

quotes: You can use the ITDR Settings section to configure safelists for AD and Entra ID issues and objects.
Safelists allow you to exclude known, trusted, or accepted issues and objects from being accounted for risk scores and reduce alert noise.
Active Directory Issue Safelist: Exclude known, accepted AD issues from posture scans and alerts.
Active Directory Object Safelist: Exclude trusted AD objects from identity issues, alerts, and posture findings.
Active Directory Change Detection Issue Safelist: Add, view, and manage safelisted change-detection issues to suppress expected alerts and focus on real identity risks.
Active Directory Change Detection Object Safelist: Exclude specific AD objects from change detection issues to reduce alert noise.
Entra ID Issue Safelist: Suppress known Entra ID findings so change detection focuses on relevant identity risks.
Entra ID Object Safelist: Exclude known safe Entra ID objects from detection to reduce false positives.
Entra ID Change Detection Issue Safelist: Suppress alerts for known Entra ID change-detection issues while maintaining visibility into real threats.
Entra ID Change Detection Object Safelist: Exclude trusted objects from Entra ID change detection so expected changes do not trigger issues.

itdr-config-agent-settings.statement: Endpoint Settings has Agents, Agent Configuration and Agent Update Groups; Server Agent Settings has Domains, Agents, Agent Update Groups and Configuration.

quotes: - Endpoint Settings
- Server Agent Settings
You can use the Endpoint Settings section to configure and control endpoint agents, monitor user systems, run targeted scans, and detect identity threats.
Agents: Monitor and manage all endpoint agents.
Agents: Monitor and manage server agents.
Agent Configuration: Customize how agents behave by renaming services, adding descriptions, automatically cleaning up duplicates.
Agent Update Groups: Control agent updates by, grouping endpoints, rolling out updates in phases, tracking update progress, and exporting update details.
You can use the Server Agent Settings section to configure and control server agents, manage domain settings, monitor authentication activity, and detect identity threats.
Domains: Manage domains and controllers to track domain health, monitor logons, identify weak or compromised passwords.
Agent Update Groups: Control server agent updates by grouping servers, managing phased rollouts, monitoring update status, etc.
Configuration: Configure server agents to detect weak passwords, set custom keywords, simulate attacks, strengthen password security locally.

authsvc-no-itdr-ui.statement: For Authentication Service-enabled customers there is no separate UI for ITDR in Authentication Service; ITDR configuration is done through the Deception UI, and the Deception tile on the Authentication Service landing page opens the ITDR Admin Portal.

quotes: There is no separate UI for ITDR in Authentication Service. The ITDR configuration is done through the Deception UI.
From the Authentication Service Landing Page, click the Deception tile to access the ITDR Admin Portal.

logout-with-authsvc.statement: With Authentication Service enabled, Logout logs the user out of the ITDR Admin Portal only, and signing in again does not require entering the user credentials.

quotes: If Authentication Service is enabled, you are logged out of the ITDR Admin Portal only. When you sign in again, you don't have to enter the user credentials.

sso-sign-in-button.statement: For an account configured with SSO, the ITDR page tells the user to click the sign-in button with the IdP name on the Sign In page, then log in at the IdP and be redirected back to the ITDR Admin Portal.

quotes: On the Sign In page, click the sign-in button with the IdP name.
If you log in successfully, you are redirected back to the ITDR Admin Portal.

nav-itdr-item.statement: On the Accessing and Navigating page, the ITDR item in the left-side navigation opens the Identity Posture, Credential Exposure and Change Detection dashboards and is where AD domain scans, credential exposure scans and threat detection policies are configured.

quotes: Click ITDR to access the Identity Posture, Credential Exposure and Change Detection dashboards. You can also configure an Active Directory (AD) domain scan, credential exposure scan and threat detection policies.

nav-system-messages.statement: In the ITDR Admin Portal the System Messages icon is described as showing audit logs and system messages, and the Account Settings icon as resetting 2FA, editing the profile, changing the time zone and changing the password.

quotes: Click the System Messages icon to view audit logs and system messages
Click the Account Settings icon to reset your two-factor authentication (2FA), edit your profile, change your time zone, and change your password.

nav-orchestrate-settings-search.statement: Orchestrate is where rules are automated, events are forwarded to SIEM and other log aggregation repositories, threats are contained, alerts are enriched and API tokens are created; Settings configures users and roles and shows license consumption and audit trails; the Search icon searches ITDR modules and sub-modules.

quotes: Automate rules to take immediate actions when events with threats are detected.
Create API tokens for additional platform integration.
Click Settings to configure users and roles and provides information regarding license consumption and audit trails.
Click the Search icon to search for ITDR modules or sub-modules across the ITDR Admin Portal.
Integrate with the security information and event management (SIEM) solutions and other log aggregation repositories to forward events to the SIEM.
Contain threats to isolate detected attackers.
Enrich alerts with relevant contextual information to the security events that are generated in the ITDR Admin Portal

investigate-landing.statement: The Investigate page is the landing page showing logged forensics and attacker information graphically, used to monitor and analyze event activities that adversaries conduct on the AD domain and endpoints.

quotes: The Investigate page is the landing page that displays all the logged forensics and attacker information in a graphical format.
monitor and analyze the event activities that adversaries conduct on the Active Directory (AD) domain and endpoints

notification-categories.statement: In the ITDR per-user Email Notifications Preferences window, Fine-Tune Notifications has License (alerts when the license is about to expire) and Security Alerts (alerts when user settings are changed, for example when a password is disabled globally).

quotes: License: Enable to generate email alert notifications when the license is about to expire.
Security Alerts: Enable to generate alerts when user settings are changed (e.g., when a password is disabled globally).

notification-preferences-account.statement: On the ITDR Account Settings page, Notification Preferences customizes email notification preferences for information relating to the license and security alerts.

quotes: Notification Preferences: Customize your email notification preferences for information relating to the license and security alerts.

predefined-roles-table.statement: The ITDR predefined roles table describes Super admin as having complete control over users, roles, APIs, modules and audit logs; Administrator as analyzing events and orchestrating actions; Analyst as investigating events, blocking or allowlisting an attacker and exporting logs; and Responder as analyzing events and orchestrating actions.

quotes: | Super admin | This role has the highest level of privilege and has complete control over users, roles, APIs, modules, audit logs, etc. |
| Administrator | Analyze events and orchestrate actions. |
| Analyst | Investigate events, block or add an attacker to an allowlist, and export logs. |
| Responder | Analyze events and orchestrate actions. |

authsvc-user-path.statement: With Authentication Service enabled, Add Users on the ITDR Users page redirects to the Authentication Service Admin Portal, where users are added under Directory > Users and assigned to the Deception service.

quotes: You are redirected to the Authentication Service Admin Portal.
Go to Directory > Users and add users and then assign the user to the Deception service.
Click Add Users.

session-timeout-time-zone.statement: In the User Details window, Time Zone sets how alert timestamps are displayed and Session Inactivity Timeout, the time after which an inactive session is logged out, is 30 minutes by default.

quotes: Time Zone: Select a time zone from the drop-down menu. Alert timestamps are displayed according to the selected time zone.
Session Inactivity Timeout: Select a time duration after which an inactive user session is logged out. By default, this is set to 30 minutes.

idp-providers-tab.statement: The ITDR Users & Roles area has an IdP Providers page (Settings > Users & Roles > IdP Providers) for configuring identity providers for SSO, and a Zscaler Remote Assistance page showing Zscaler Support users with Read-only or Admin role.

quotes: On the IdP Providers page (Settings > Users & Roles > IdP Providers), you can configure identity providers (IdPs) to support single sign-on (SSO) for users in ITDR.
Role: The role (Read-only or Admin) assigned to the user.
On the Zscaler Remote Assistance page (Settings > Users & Roles > Zscaler Remote Assistance), you can view the details of Zscaler Support users who can access the ITDR Admin Portal.

table-export.statement: Table data in the ITDR Admin Portal can be exported or downloaded as a CSV or JSON file using the Export as CSV, Download as CSV or Download as JSON options in the Actions drop-down menu.

quotes: You can export or download data from a table as a CSV or JSON file.
Select Export as CSV, Download as CSV, or Download as JSON from the Actions drop-down menu to download data from the table to your system.

table-copy-limit.statement: Copy Table in the Actions menu copies chosen columns from tables, up to 1,000 rows, to the clipboard for pasting into CSV, JSON, Notepad or other compatible files.

quotes: You can copy specific columns from tables (up to 1,000 rows) and paste them into CSV, JSON, Notepad, or other compatible files.
Click Copy Table from the Actions drop-down menu.

table-where-used.statement: The Using Tables page names Detailed Findings and Recommendations, Change Detection and Scan Reports as pages where data is shown in tables.

quotes: Data is organized and displayed in tables on some of the pages (e.g., Detailed Findings and Recommendations, Change Detection, Scan Reports, etc.)

query-modules.statement: The ITDR query-language page lists Filter in Dashboard, Conditions in Orchestration Rules and Event Filters in SIEM Integrations as modules where it builds custom conditions or filters; its I-flag note still mentions ThreatParse rules in Miragemaker as a place the flag can be used.

quotes: You can use the query language to build custom conditions or filters in the following modules:
Filter in Dashboard
Conditions in Orchestration Rules
Event Filters in SIEM Integrations

This flag is not supported in the Filters in Dashboard. However, you can use it in regular expression queries in conditions in Orchestration Rules, event filters in SIEM Integrations, and ThreatParse rules in Miragemaker.

query-editor-locations.statement: The query editor is on the Investigate dashboard (interactive query builder at the top), in the Rule Details window reached from Orchestrate > Rules, and in the SIEM integration details window reached from Orchestrate > SIEM Integrations.

quotes: Under Investigate, an interactive query builder is located on the top of the dashboard to filter dashboard items.
To access the Rule Details window, go to Orchestrate > Rules, and add (by clicking Add Rule) or edit (by clicking the edit icon) a rule.
To access the respective SIEM integration details window, go to Orchestrate > SIEM Integrations

advanced-settings-tabs.statement: The ITDR Advanced Settings page is described as letting you view license details, manage event logs and configure a retention policy for logs; its Manage Events & Evidence tab exports events as serializable JSON for a From/To window and deletes either all events or only those marked as safe for a window.

quotes: Advanced Settings allow you to view license details, manage events logs, configure a retention policy for logs, and more.
under Export Events (Serializable JSON), select a date and time from the From and To drop-down menus.
All Events: All the events for the specified time frame are deleted.
Marked as safe only: Only events that are marked as safe are deleted.
Go to Settings > Advanced Settings.

license-tab-fields.statement: The ITDR License tab shows Client, Plan, Expiration, Retention Policy, Decoys (configured out of the plan total), Landmine Users (configured out of the plan total) and Admin Portal Version.

quotes: Client: The customer name the license is issued to.
Plan: The active ITDR subscription plan your organization is licensed to.
Retention Policy: The number of days after which all events and evidence files are permanently deleted.
Decoys: The number of decoys configured out of the total decoys included in your subscription plan.
Landmine Users: The number of users that have landmine configured out of the total landmine users included in your subscription plan.
Admin Portal Version: The current version of ITDR.
Expiration: The expiration date of your current subscribed license.

retention-values.statement: The ITDR retention policy defaults to 365 days and can be reduced; events marked as safe are retained for 7 days and Okta system logs for threat detection for 14 days, and the page says the retention period of those events or logs cannot be modified.

quotes: The default retention period is 365 days, and it can be reduced if required.
The retention period of the following events or logs cannot be modified
Events that are marked as safe are retained for 7 days.
Okta system logs for threat detection are retained for 14 days.

logs-page-tabs.statement: The ITDR Logs page (Settings > Logs) has Audit Logs (exportable as CSV, with Timestamp, Username, Module and Description), error logs (with Timestamp, Category, Module, Message, Metadata, Error, Count and Actions) and Debug Logs (downloadable for the last 2 hours, 24 hours or 7 days).

quotes: On the Logs page (Settings > Logs), you can see the following tabs:
You can export audit logs as a CSV file.
Category: The component (Containment, Enrichment, etc.) which caused the error.
Count: The number of times the error occurred.
You can download debug logs for the last 2 hours, 24 hours, or 7 days.
Timestamp: The time when the user activity occurred.
Username: The ID of the user who performed the activity.
Module: The ITDR module (Login, Retention Policy, etc.) on which the activity occurred.
Description: The description of the activity.
Timestamp: The time when the error occurred.
Module: The ITDR entity (ZPA, Email, etc.) on which the error occurred.
Message: A brief explanation of the error.
Metadata: The metadata that provides context about the error.
Error: Hover over the information icon to view the error message.
Actions: Click the Delete icon to delete the message, or click the checkmark to mark the message as read.

debug-log-download.statement: Requesting debug logs creates an archive for the chosen time range, which is ready to download after a couple of minutes.

quotes: Click Request to create an archive file with the logs for the requested time range.
When the debug logs are ready to download after a couple of minutes, click the here link.

account-settings-2fa-password.statement: The ITDR Account Settings page states that Reset 2FA and Change Password are available only if the Disable Password Login option was selected while adding a user.

quotes: The Reset 2FA and Change Password actions are available only if the Disable Password Login option is selected while adding a user.

reset-2fa-steps.statement: Resetting 2FA is done on the Account Settings page by entering the password and the current 2FA code from the authenticator app, scanning a new QR code and submitting the 6-digit one-time password.

quotes: Enter your Password and the Current 2FA code that appears on the authenticator app.
When a QR code appears, scan it using an authenticator app.
This is the 6-digit code shown on the authenticator app.
On the Accounts Settings page, under Two-Factor Authentication, click Reset 2FA.
Click Submit OTP.

first-sign-in-eusa.statement: The page's "Accepting the End User Subscription Agreement (EUSA)" item, which follows its "For Customers Using SSO" section, says the ITDR Admin Portal displays an EUSA at first login that must be accepted to activate the license; the provisioning email contains a link to the ITDR instance, a link to set the password and a security code.

quotes: You cannot activate your license without accepting the EUSA.
Accepting the End User Subscription Agreement (EUSA)
For Customers Using SSO
Link to set your password
Security code
When you log in for the first time, the ITDR Admin Portal displays an EUSA. Click Accept to accept the EUSA.
After your organization is provisioned for Zscaler ITDR, you will receive an email with the following details:
Link to your Zscaler ITDR instance

investigate-dashboard-filters.statement: On the ITDR Investigate page, alerts can be filtered with queries and predefined time ranges, and the dashboard can be customized by filtering events on level of details and threat level.

quotes: Filter the events shown in the alerts area using queries and predefined time ranges.
Customize the dashboard by filtering events based on level of details, threat level, etc.

investigate-details-pane-objects.statement: The ITDR copy says the details pane is unique for each Zscaler ITDR object (Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal, Decoy Connector, Decoy Group and Decoy) and attacker; the object pane shows triggered ThreatParse rules and attacker risk scores.

quotes: The details pane is unique for each Zscaler ITDR object (Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal, Decoy Connector, Decoy Group, and Decoy) and attacker.
The object details pane shows you ThreatParse rules that are triggered by attackers connecting to that object, and includes the risk scores assigned to attackers.

investigate-attacker-pane.statement: The attacker details pane shows the attacker's risk score, first and last event timestamps, triggered ThreatParse rules and any triage incidents from the endpoint if available, and its Actions menu can contain, block or delete threats or mark an attack as safe.

quotes: The attacker details pane shows you the risk score associated with the attacker, along with the first and last event timestamp.
any triage incidents from the endpoint, if available.
Click Actions to contain, block, or delete threats. You can also mark an attack as safe.
It shows you a list of ThreatParse rules triggered by the attacker

investigate-containment-targets.statement: The ITDR Actions menu can forward an attacker's details to CrowdStrike Falcon Insight, Amazon GuardDuty, Threat Protection with Okta AI, Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA), after the settings for these tools are enabled on the Containment page.

quotes: Forward the attacker's details to the following security tools or services to remediate the issue:
CrowdStrike Falcon Insight
Amazon GuardDuty
Threat Protection with Okta AI
Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA)
Zscaler Private Access (ZPA)
Before forwarding the attacker's details, make sure to enable the settings for these tools on the Containment page.

investigate-mark-safe-behavior.statement: Marking an event as safe removes the attacker from the default view; when an attacker is marked as safe it can take up to an hour to show; marking an attacker's IP address as safe marks all past events from it as safe while new events from that IP are still generated and displayed; Show marked as safe is enabled from the Select Query drop-down menu.

quotes: You can mark an event as safe by selecting the Mark as safe option. This removes the attacker from the default view in the Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.
When an attacker is marked as safe, it can take up to an hour for the action to be reflected in the ITDR Admin Portal depending on the number of events associated with the attacker.

If you mark an attacker's IP address as safe, all the past events from that attacker are marked as safe. However, any new events from that IP address are generated and displayed on the Zscaler ITDR dashboard.
Click the Select Query drop-down menu and enable Show marked as safe.

investigate-delete-attacker.statement: Deleting an attacker removes all previously triggered events related to it and permanently deletes the ThreatParse data linked to it, while the tags associated with the attacker are retained; the blocklist option redirects to the Blocklist page to create a rule.

quotes: When you delete an attacker, all previously triggered events related to the attacker's activities are removed from the ITDR Admin Portal, and any associated ThreatParse data linked to the attacker is also permanently deleted.
Tags associated with the attacker are retained.
When you select the blocklist option, you are redirected to the Blocklist page to create the rule.

investigate-extended-details-tabs.statement: In the ITDR copy, View Extended Details shows the tabs ThreatParse (attack details mapped to MITRE ATT&CK with a risk score), Chronology (temporal overview and heatmap) and Event Logs.

quotes: The following tabs are displayed:
ThreatParse: Attack details based on the MITRE ATT&CK framework along with a risk score in plain English.
Chronology: A temporal overview and heatmap of the attacker's activities.
Event Logs: Event logs associated with an attacker activity.

investigate-extended-details-elements.statement: The ITDR extended-details intro says attacker activities are recorded as events and that you can evaluate the attacker's actions and how they interact with the Zscaler ITDR elements, naming endpoint credentials and Entra ID.

quotes: You can evaluate the attacker's actions and how they interact with the Zscaler ITDR elements (endpoint credentials, Entra ID).
Attacker activities are recorded as events and displayed as a graph on the Investigate page.

investigate-event-log-delete-and-test.statement: On the ITDR Event Logs page, Delete All removes at most 100K events at a time, deleting selected events works well when there are fewer than 100 events, and Test Rule accepts a maximum of 10 selected events.

quotes: The option to delete specific events works well when the number of events is less than 100.
The Delete All option removes a maximum of 100K events at a time.
You can select a maximum of 10 events.

investigate-event-log-export-and-columns.statement: ITDR Event Logs can be exported as Attacker Summary in JSON or CSV, Events as JSON, Event Fields as JSON, Events as CSV, STIX v1.2, STIX v2.1 and Snort Rules, and up to 50 columns can be added to the table.

quotes: Attacker Summary in JSON: Export a JSON file
Attacker Summary in CSV: Export a CSV file
Events as JSON: Export a JSON file that includes all fields for event logs.
Event Fields as JSON: Export a JSON file that includes all fields for event fields.
Events as CSV: Export a CSV file
STIX v1.2: Export a file in STIX format
STIX v2.1: Export a file in STIX format
Snort Rules: Export a file that includes the snort rules for the event logs.
You can add a maximum of 50 columns.

investigate-event-log-columns.statement: The ITDR Event Logs basic event information lists Timestamp, Attack Type, Attacker ID (the attacker's IP address), Decoy Name, Decoy Group, Decoy Port, Decoy Connector and Kill Chain Phase.

quotes: Timestamp: The time and date when the attack happened.
Attack Type: The attack type (e.g., network, web, etc.).
Attacker ID: The attacker's IP address.
Decoy Name: The name of the decoy with which the attacker interacted.
Decoy Group: The category of decoy on which the attacker attacks.
Decoy Port: The port number of the decoy.
Decoy Connector: The name of the Decoy Connector.
Kill Chain Phase: The kill chain attack phase

investigate-chronology-threatparse.statement: The Chronology page has an events-over-time graph and an activity-over-a-week heatmap in which a brighter spot represents a high volume of activity.

quotes: Events over time graph:

Activity over a week graph: This graph shows a heatmap that helps you to analyze the attacker's activity pattern for a weekly duration. A brighter spot on the graph represents a high volume of activity.

itdr-config-where-managed.summary: One page says ITDR settings are at Identities > ITDR Config with detailed configuration managed in the legacy ITDR Admin Portal; another says Identity Protection is managed through the SecOps Settings page, with some links redirecting to the legacy experience for deeper configuration.

quotes: While the ITDR Config page is available on the SecOps platform, the detailed configuration is managed in the legacy Zscaler ITDR Admin Portal.

positions.says: The ITDR Config page is on the SecOps platform, but the detailed configuration is managed in the legacy ITDR Admin Portal.

quotes: Within the Settings page, you can adjust scan configurations and review clear explanations for each option.
When deeper configuration is required, certain links redirect you to the legacy ITDR experience

positions.says: The SecOps Settings page adjusts scan configurations; only when deeper configuration is required do certain links redirect to the legacy ITDR experience.

itdr-config-where-managed.impact: The pages name different places (ITDR Config page versus Settings page) and different extents of what stays in the legacy portal (detailed configuration versus deeper configuration reached through some links); neither says whether they are the same page or how the two scopes compare.

advanced-settings-evidence.title: Whether ITDR has the evidence-file and internal-component sections of the Deception Advanced Settings page
advanced-settings-evidence.detail: The ITDR Advanced Settings page has no Download an Evidence File, Delete an Evidence File or Show/Hide Internal Components sections, while its License tab still lists Decoys and Landmine Users; whether those controls exist in ITDR is not stated.

extended-details-tabs.title: Whether ITDR has the Network and Evidence tabs on View Extended Details
extended-details-tabs.detail: The ITDR page lists ThreatParse, Chronology and Event Logs; the Deception page lists ThreatParse, Chronology, Network, Event Logs and Evidence. Whether ITDR omits Network and Evidence in the product or only on the page is not stated.
